_: MARKET EVIDENCE — what comparable programmes actually charge.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
The ten-year model identified its own weakest point and said so in
writing: segment willingness-to-pay was MODELLED and not researched,
and everything downstream — $61.6M of revenue, $14.1M of surplus —
rested on it. This file is the research that was done in answer.
EVERY ROW CARRIES ITS SOURCE. A figure without a URL and a date is
not evidence, and none appears below. Where the research did not
find a reliable public figure, the gap is recorded as a gap and the
assumption that fills it is marked
MODELLED — INSUFFICIENT DIRECT MARKET EVIDENCE
rather than dressed up with a number that looks researched. Several
of the most interesting entries below are of exactly that kind: the
premium providers in Saudi Arabia do not publish prices at all, and
that refusal is itself a finding about the segment.
THE COMPARISON THAT MATTERS IS NOT HEADLINE TUITION
A cheaper English course existing somewhere does not make WEC-LC
overpriced, and an expensive one existing does not make it cheap.
The comparison that carries information is PRICE PER HOUR OF
INDIVIDUAL INSTRUCTOR ATTENTION, because attention is the only
thing any of these providers actually spends money on.
A group class of twelve at 90 contact hours gives each learner 7.5
hours of an instructor's attention. A WEC-LC Tutored level gives
roughly 16 hours per learner — six individual tutorial hours, a
share of the group hours, and six hours of a person reading and
answering produced work. Those are the units this file compares.
Researched 19 September 2026. Currency conversions at the rates
noted; they move, and a figure quoted in its own currency is the
durable one.

_: Two different markets are often conflated here, and the difference
decides WEC-LC's executive tariff.
EXECUTIVE COACHING — leadership, not language — runs $200–$600 an
hour with a median near $500. EXECUTIVE LANGUAGE TRAINING runs far
below that: $50–$120 an hour for one to one.
WEC-LC executive sits between them: it is language delivered one to
one, but it terminates in a verifiable credential rather than in a
set of sessions. Pricing it at coaching rates would be borrowing
credibility from a different market; pricing it at corporate
language rates would ignore the qualification.

observations.note: Quoted as the upper reference, NOT as a WEC-LC comparable. WEC-LC does not sell leadership coaching.
Marketplace tutors, no credential, no assessment, no institution behind them.

gaps.topic: Willingness to pay for a MULTI-YEAR credentialed English pathway
gaps.note: This is the honest centre of the problem. No provider found sells a six-level, 1,200-hour, credentialed A1–C2 pathway as one purchase. Every comparable is either a single level, a test preparation course, or a university pre-sessional. WEC-LC's product does not have a market price because the product is not on the market. The pathway prices below are therefore built UP from per-level comparables rather than read off a competitor.
